guide.summary: Roman, art and science museums, a cathedral, a covered market and a city park, with bouchon-era tables, bakeries, cafés and bars checked against their own websites.
highlights: Les Halles de Lyon Paul Bocuse
guide.tip: Plan around closing days: the Musée des Beaux-Arts shuts on Tuesdays and public holidays, Gadagne opens only Wednesday to Sunday, and La Mère Brazier serves only Monday to Friday.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: The Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon is closed on Tuesdays and public holidays, and Musées Gadagne opens Wednesday to Sunday only. The Maison des Canuts opens Tuesday to Saturday and closes on public holidays.

toolkit.label: Tickets
toolkit.copy: The Musée des Confluences recommends buying tickets online to avoid queues and stays open until 22:00 on the first Thursday of the month. The Aquarium de Lyon says no booking is needed for general visits.

toolkit.label: Restaurant days
toolkit.copy: La Mère Brazier serves Monday to Friday only, and Takao Takano opens Monday evening and Tuesday to Friday. Paul Bocuse at Collonges serves Wednesday to Sunday.

toolkit.label: Dress and rules
toolkit.copy: Têtedoie's gastronomic room asks men to wear trousers and closed shoes, and Paul Bocuse asks for smart dress. At Parc de la Tête d'Or, entry is barred a quarter-hour before closing.

guide.dek: Anchor each day on one museum with fixed closing days, then book the weekday-only restaurants first.
intro: Lyon rewards you for planning around opening days. The Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon on place des Terreaux opens Wednesday to Monday and closes on Tuesdays and public holidays, while Musées Gadagne in Vieux Lyon, home to the city history and puppet museums, opens Wednesday to Sunday from 10:30 to 18:00. Across the Saône, the Cathédrale Saint-Jean-Baptiste opens every day, from 14:00 on Mondays. Up the hill, Lugdunum's museum opens Tuesday to Sunday, and its Roman theatres open from 7:00 to 19:00 through the winter season.

Several exhibitions run well into next year. At the Musée des Beaux-Arts, Musée sentimental runs from 11 September 2026 to 14 March 2027, and the Biennale de Lyon is on until 13 December 2026. The Musée des Confluences shows Animal culte until 15 August 2027 and Corée du Nord until 2 January 2028, with a late opening to 22:00 on the first Thursday of each month. At the Grand Hôtel-Dieu, an Alphonse Mucha exhibition runs to 24 January 2027, and the courtyards and gardens open daily from 7:30.

For food, start at Les Halles de Lyon Paul Bocuse on cours Lafayette, but note its warning that Mondays are a rest day for many traders. Book the classic tables early: La Mère Brazier on rue Royale serves Monday to Friday only, Paul Bocuse at Collonges serves Wednesday to Sunday, and Têtedoie on rue Pierre Marion runs a gastronomic room, closed Tuesdays, beside a bistrot open daily. Brasserie Georges by Perrache opens seven days a week and takes online bookings.

Mornings are easy. Sébastien Bouillet's Boulangerie du Palais in Vieux Lyon opens daily from 7:00, and Café Bouillet on boulevard de la Croix-Rousse opens from 8:00. Slake runs coffee shops in the Jacobins and Terreaux areas from 8:00. In Croix-Rousse, the Maison des Canuts runs guided silk-workshop tours Tuesday to Saturday at 11:00 and 15:30. With children, the Aquarium de Lyon opens daily from 10:30 without booking, and Parc de la Tête d'Or keeps winter hours of 6:30 to 20:30.
summaryCards: Pair the Cathédrale Saint-Jean-Baptiste and Musées Gadagne in Vieux Lyon with an afternoon at the Musée des Confluences.
Start with a coffee at Café Bouillet, then take the 11:00 guided tour at the Maison des Canuts, Tuesday to Saturday.
La Mère Brazier closes at weekends and the Musée des Beaux-Arts closes on Tuesdays, so set those days first.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. The Basilique Notre-Dame de Fourvière was left out only because its official site publishes no street address; its site was active and showed its gardens closed to 30 October 2026 for tower works. Sites that could not be read: Café des Fédérations (expired certificate), Le Bouchon des Filles (connection reset), Pralus (rate-limited), Cour des Loges (403), and Food Traboule (domain redirects elsewhere). Partially published: Institut Lumière, Villa Florentine, Fourvière Hôtel and Brasserie Georges show no hours on the pages read; Les Halles publishes stall hours rather than market hours; Le Sucre's hours vary by event. Several restaurants (La Mère Brazier, Takao Takano, Paul Bocuse, Bernachon, Slake) were confirmed by live booking or current hours rather than dated 2026 content.
